Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Solara Energy Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. Instructions for those joining by phone: If you have a question, press star then one on your telephone keypad. If you're using speaker equipment, please pick up your handset before pressing the keys. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Solara Energy's results for the third quarter. Joining me on today's call are Elena Vasquez, Chief Executive Officer; Marcus Hale, Chief Financial Officer; Jordan Lee, Chief Development Officer; Dr. Nina Patel, Chief Technology Officer; and Liam Chen, Chief Sustainability Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements. We encourage you to review the disclaimer in our press release and on our website regarding these statements.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Elena Vasquez.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. We are pleased to report a strong Q3 performance, driven by our continued focus on innovation, operational excellence, and sustainability. We are seeing strong demand for our renewable energy solutions across all markets.

Here are six key highlights from the quarter:

First, we executed exceptionally on our financing strategy, closing $1.2 billion in new tax equity and project-level financings that fully funded our near-term construction starts and lowered our cost of capital significantly.

Second, our capacity factor performance across solar, wind, and storage technologies exceeded expectations, with fleet-wide averages improving markedly due to advanced optimizations and hybrid deployments.

Third, we added a record amount to our development pipeline and achieved critical project milestones, including multiple CODs and PPA executions that de-risked substantial capacity.

Fourth, we raised our capacity addition guidance for next year, supported by ambitious pipeline targets that position us for sustained growth amid robust market tailwinds.

Fifth, our capital expenditures and operating expenses demonstrated strong efficiency, with CAPEX front-loaded into high-return projects and OPEX compressed through scalable operations.

Sixth, capital recycling via asset sales generated substantial proceeds, enabling us to recycle equity into our greenfield pipeline without added dilution.

Now, I will turn the call over to Marcus Hale to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Marcus Hale:
Thank you, Elena. We are very pleased with our financial performance in Q3. Revenue was $450 million, a 25% increase year-over-year. This increase was driven by higher project commissioning and energy sales. Gross margin was 45%, reflecting improved cost management and favorable pricing. Operating expenses were $120 million, primarily due to increased investments in R&D and sales and marketing. Net income was $85 million, or $0.72 per share. We ended the quarter with $1.2 billion in cash and cash equivalents. We are reaffirming our full-year guidance for revenue and earnings.

Before moving on, let me expand on a few of these drivers, starting with our financing execution, particularly tax equity financing and project-level financing, which remain the foundation of our capital stack as we scale our 15 GW development pipeline in solar PV, onshore wind, and utility-scale battery storage. In Q3, we closed $1.2 billion in new financings, lifting year-to-date totals to $4.8 billion—a 35% year-over-year rise—that completely funds our upcoming construction phases.

Tax equity financing continues to excel in monetizing enhanced tax credits from the Inflation Reduction Act. Investors such as major U.S. banks including JPMorgan Chase, Wells Fargo, and US Bancorp, plus insurers like Prudential and MetLife, supply non-debt capital for a portion of the project's Investment Tax Credit, Production Tax Credit, or the new Clean Electricity versions. This is vital for developers like Solara Energy, letting us transfer 100% of credits through elective pay or direct transferability—a major IRA innovation.

Specifically in Q3, we locked in $850 million in tax equity for four projects: the 450 MW Desert Sun solar-plus-storage in Arizona, 300 MW Wind Ridge onshore wind in Texas, and two 200 MW BESS setups in California with bifacial TOPCon solar. These formed a blended 38% tax equity slice of project costs, using a flip structure where investors initially hold 45-55% economic interest to capture the full 30% base ITC plus up to 20% adders for domestic content—we achieved 85% U.S.-sourced modules from First Solar and Hanwha Q CELLS—and energy communities. After 5-7 years, once credits are harvested, control returns to us after investors hit a 7-8% unlevered IRR.

Investor demand is booming, with tax equity availability up 25% industry-wide in 2024 according to BDO's Renewable Energy Tax Equity Market Update, thanks to $369 billion in IRA credits. We secured average pre-tax IRRs of 7.2%, down from 8.5% last year, aided by softer 10-year Treasury yields and our low-risk assets. The Southwest U.S., especially Texas and Arizona, drove 60% of closings with superior solar economics and ERCOT storage premiums. In Europe, for our 2 GW Irish offshore wind, we're mirroring this with EU Renewable Energy Directive III partners like Allianz and ING.

Overall, this drops our weighted average cost of capital to 5.1% on financed projects, versus 6.8% using just corporate debt. We've broadened to 40% non-bank investors like Google and Amazon via TCJA Section 48E, countering bank limits from Basel III. Ahead, our 5 GW backlog has $3.2 billion queued in tax equity, with initial closings for our 800 MW Nevada solar in Q1 2025, grabbing the full 70% ITC via prevailing wage.

On project-level financing, this non-recourse debt layer is secured by PPAs, offtake, and contracts, matching project timelines from construction loans to term debt at COD. Q3 saw $2.1 billion closed for 1.2 GW, like a $650 million facility for Desert Sun from MUFG and DNB at SOFR + 145 bps (5.9% all-in), and $450 million back-leverage on our 250 MW California BESS from Macquarie and Rabobank.

Our stack is typically 40-45% tax equity/sponsor equity, 50-55% project debt, and 5-10% back-leverage. Debt hits 60-65% DSCR minimums, with 75% advance rates on fixed EPC from Turner Renewable Energy and Quanta Services. Trends align with $550 billion global green bonds in 2024 per Climate Bonds Initiative, though project finance rules U.S. utilities post-FERC Order 2023.

In the U.S. Southwest, PG&E and APS PPAs at $35-45/MWh fixed yield 28-32% solar capacity factors with N-type TOPCon from Array Technologies. Midwest wind tapped Euler Hermes for Vestas turbines at L+175 bps despite steel tariffs. Australia's 400 MW Queensland solar used BBSW + 200 bps kangaroo bonds post-AEMO reforms.

Metrics: 18-year average tenor post-COD, 95% fixed via swaps against Fed moves, 4.2x DSCR on stabilized assets for 12-14% IRRs. Supply chain hikes lifted BOS 8% YoY, but 2% PPA escalators and CAISO $100/kW ancillaries buffer. Together, this recycled $1.5 billion sponsor equity in Q3, covering 70% of 2025 starts. FY25 targets $7-8 billion financings, tax equity to 42% with IRA 45X from our Nevada First Solar JV. Risks like policy shifts are offset by bipartisan siting (80% red states) and storage hybrids.

Turning to capital expenditures and operating expenses, which underpin our execution. In Q3, CAPEX hit $623 million, up 28% YoY and 12% sequentially, pushing trailing twelve months to $2.1 billion toward full-year $2.4-2.6 billion guidance. This front-loads our CIP backlog amid low module/steel costs.

65% or $405 million built core assets: $ for 1.2 GW Texas Crescent solar with perovskite-silicon JV for 10% LCOE gains, 25% for 400 MW Midwest wind with Vestas 15 MW turbines. 20% or $125 million scaled 300 MWh California BESS for ITC adders. 10% or $62 million advanced 50 MW Dutch PEM electrolyzer for EU Hydrogen Bank. 5% or $31 million for land, permits, Siemens digital twins.

U.S. took 55% ($342M) via IRA; Europe 30% ($187M) despite German delays; APAC 15%. Efficiency: EPC to $0.92/W, 8% YoY drop with 45% domestic content. 2025 CAPEX $2.8 billion for 3 GW at 12%+ ROIC.

OPEX was $178 million, up 4% YoY but flat sequentially, 22% of revenue versus 24% prior. OPEX guidance $720-750 million, margins to 35-38%. Cost of revenue $98 million (55%) cut downtime 22% via drones/AI SCADA; in-house techs limit third-parties. SG&A $45 million (25%), 5.6% revenue; R&D $35 million (20%) on TOPCon, flow batteries, H2—150 patents.

U.S. OPEX $28/MW-year; Europe $42/MW-year; APAC $35/MW-year. This funds 20% GW ramp at 2.8x net debt/EBITDA.

Finally, capital recycling and asset sales: Q3 closed $850 million, YTD $2.1 billion up 45%, funding 1.5 GW 2025 builds. We sell stabilized assets with predictable flows to infra funds like BlackRock, Brookfield, CPP.

Q3 stars: 350 MW Sunbelt Solar in ERCOT to I Squared for $520 million (12.2x EBITDA), 18% IRR; 150 MW Northeast Wind to Octopus for $330 million (11.8x). YTD $1.2 billion gains lift ROIC to 11.4%, deleverage to 3.8x.

U.S. 70%, IRA speeds deals; CAISO hybrids up 20%; Europe 25%; LatAm 5%. 'Revive & Recycle' repowers 500 MW wind + 200 MWh BESS boosts multiples 15-20%. H1 2025: $1.5 billion queued, 25-30% FFO CAGR.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan Lee for an update on our project pipeline.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Marcus. Our project pipeline continues to grow, with 15 GW under development. We are making good progress on securing land rights, obtaining permits, and negotiating power purchase agreements. In Q3, we added a record 12.4 GW net new capacity, pushing totals to 58.7 GW across solar PV, onshore/offshore wind, and BESS/hybrids—a 28% sequential jump, top-tier with NextEra and Orsted. YTD, 85% of targets hit, ahead 12 points via land and permits.

Solar: 7.2 GWdc added, 58%, including 1.5 GW U.S. Southwest agrivoltaics in Arizona. Wind: 3.8 GW, 2.1 GW onshore U.S. Plains with Vestas 15 MW, 1.7 GW offshore East Coast like Empire Wind 2. BESS: 1.4 GW/4.2 GWh, 800 MW/2.4 GWh hybrids with Tesla Megapacks under FERC 2222.

U.S. 65% (38 GW), $2.1 billion Q3 tax equity; Europe 20% (11.7 GW), UK/Germany auctions; APAC/LatAm 10-15%, India 500 MW, Chile 300 MW.

Milestones: 22 CODs for 4.8 GW, $1.2 billion revenue; ACUB for 1.2 GW solar; PJM queue advances 3.5 GW; 15 PPAs at $42/MWh solar, $38/MWh wind, $65/kW-year storage; $3.8 billion financing; NTP on 6.2 GW like 1.1 GW Texas Solara del Desierto, 400 MW California BESS.

45% new adds are RE+ hybrids for < $25/MWh LCOE; $450 million brownfield repowers; 80% 2025-26 supply secured. H2: 10-12 GW adds, 8 GW NTP; 5+ years visibility at 15-20% CAGR.

We expect to bring several new projects online in the coming quarters. We are also actively exploring opportunities to expand our project portfolio through strategic acquisitions and partnerships.

On capacity addition guidance and pipeline targets, for FY2025 we're raising to 3.2-3.6 GW operational, 25% YoY growth from 2.6 GW 2024. Solar 2.1-2.4 GWdc (Gemini 500 MW Q1); wind 800 MW-1 GW; BESS 300-400 MW/1.2-1.6 GWh. Capex $3.2-3.5 billion, 60% tax equity.

Pipeline at 28 GW: 8.2 GW contracted (India 1.2 GW, Oklahoma repowers); 12.5 GW late-stage hybrids; 7.3 GW early like Australia NEM, Iberia. U.S. 65%, Europe 15%, APAC 12%, LatAm 8%. YE2025 target 35 GW via AI O&M, 70% storage, $500M M&A.

Next, Dr. Patel will provide an update on our technology initiatives.

Dr. Nina Patel:
Thank you, Jordan. We are committed to developing and deploying innovative technologies that improve the efficiency and reliability of renewable energy systems. We are making significant progress on our research and development efforts, including advanced solar panel technologies, energy storage solutions, and smart grid technologies. We believe that these technologies will play a critical role in accelerating the transition to a clean energy future. The development of advanced bifacial solar panels is expected to have substantial efficiency improvements on our future projects.

Delving into capacity factor performance by technology, our fleet-wide average rose to 34.2% YoY from 31.8%, topping NREL by 250 bps and peers, fueling 42% EBITDA margins and 12-14% IRRs.

Solar PV (4.2 GW, 28 projects): 28.4% average, +180 bps, from 1.8 GW bifacial PERC/TOPCon. Southwest (60%) 32.1% with Array Nextracker; Australia 26.8% via AI soiling; APAC 22.5%, perovskite pilots for +5%. PVsyst/NOAA cuts losses 12%; 2 GW HJT pipeline for 30%+.

Wind (3.5 GW, 70/30 onshore/offshore): 41.2% blended, +220 bps. Onshore (2.45 GW) 37.8%, Vestas V150 at 42% Iowa, 34% German; Offshore (1.05 GW) 52.6%, Siemens SG 14-222 at 55% Moray East. Curtailment 5% U.S., +10% Europe dispatch; 15 MW+ for 55-60%.

Storage (2.8 GWh LFP): 68.4% effective, 92.3% RTE, $150M ancillaries. Standalone 62%, hybrids 72%, LDES pilots 45%. Texas 75%, UK 80%; <0.5% degradation.

Hybrids at 42% CF unlock $35-45/MWh PPAs; $200M digital twins for +300 bps by 2026. Risks hedged, 15% FCF CAGR.

And now, Liam Chen will provide an update on our sustainability efforts.

Liam Chen:
Thank you, Dr. Patel. We are committed to operating our business in a sustainable manner and minimizing our environmental impact. We have set ambitious goals for reducing our carbon emissions, improving our energy efficiency, and promoting responsible resource management. We are also actively involved in community engagement and supporting local initiatives that promote sustainability. We believe that sustainability is not only the right thing to do but also makes good business sense.

I'll now turn the call back to Elena for closing remarks.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Liam. In closing, we are confident that Solara Energy is well-positioned to capitalize on the growing demand for renewable energy. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and delivering long-term value for our shareholders.

Operator, let's open the line for questions.

Operator:
Instructions for the question-and-answer session: If you have a question, press star one. Our first question comes from Sarah Thompson with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson:
Can you provide more details on the regulatory environment for renewable energy projects in your key markets?

Elena Vasquez:
Thanks, Sarah. The regulatory landscape remains supportive overall, particularly in the U.S. with IRA extensions bolstering ITC/PTC transferability and FERC reforms like Order 2023 and 2222 clearing queues and enabling storage. In ERCOT and CAISO, duck curve mandates favor hybrids, while PJM's energized lineups have accelerated our 3.5 GW. Europe benefits from REPowerEU's 320 GW solar push and Hydrogen Bank auctions, though German grid delays persist—we're mitigating via offshore like Ireland. Risks like election shifts are buffered by 80% red-state siting and bipartisan storage focus. Globally, Australia's AEMO and India's 500 GW targets align perfectly.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Mike Chen:
How is the company addressing the challenges of energy storage integration with your renewable energy projects?

Dr. Nina Patel:
Great question, Mike. Storage integration is core to our hybrids, now 45-70% of pipeline. We're deploying 4-hour LFP Megapacks co-located for 72% CF uplift, smoothing solar/wind variance to 4.8% daily via Stem AI. Challenges like degradation (<0.5% post-2,000 cycles) and dispatch are tackled with 95% RTE active cooling, FERC 2222 ancillaries ($100/kW CAISO), and LDES pilots like iron-air for 100-hour. Roadmap: 1 GWh more, qualifying full ITC adders, targeting 90% dispatchability for AI data centers. Digital twins predict maintenance, cutting downtime.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Patel with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Lisa Patel:
What are your expectations for the long-term growth of the renewable energy market?

Elena Vasquez:
Lisa, we're bullish long-term. BNEF sees 500 GW global adds in 2024, EIA 50 GW U.S. annual to 2030, driven by hyperscalers' 50 GW AI demand, RE100, and LCOEs at $20-30/MWh undercutting gas. IRA's $370B, EU's €800B funds, India's 500 GW sustain this. Our 58.7 GW pipeline, 15-20% CAGR, CF edge, recycling flywheel position us for 2-3% U.S. share, 20% FFO growth to 2028, outpacing peers.

Operator:
Instructions confirmed. There appear to be no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back over to Elena Vasquez for any closing remarks.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, everyone, for joining us today. We appreciate your interest in Solara Energy. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
